about: CHAIN house_rival (Design/content/chains/house_rival.md): the rival Frisian house of Dorestad, 795 to about 808, with an epilogue for the heirs from 826. Thirteen cards. Thiadbod (spine cast.thiadbod), the biggest shipman on the river, undersells the player's house (short cloaks, a short corn measure), takes its berth, and has its boat cut from her post by night; the case goes to the count's court under the Frisians' own law; later his ship lies on a bank and the player decides what to do; three endings (partnership, ruin, feud), and a feud that the heirs inherit. Progress is flags ch_house_rival_1 to _9; branch flags, endings and grand rewards are listed in the chain page. Scheduled cards have weight 0 and are reached only by 'schedule' (their 'when' says when they belong; the scheduler does not read it). The chain gives way to chain house_debt: if the tally was sold to Thiadbod (the spine's flag db_bought) steps 1 and 3 do not come. The words are in Data/writing/chain_house_rival.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text (the engine shows the effects' own facts; the outcome keys are for the integrator). Law: Lex Frisionum (text and titles as in Herold 1557, read in K. Nieuwenhuijsen's edition at keesn.nl/lex); capitularies as in chronicle_793.json. Written 4 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Dorestad once the house has made a few calls and has some silver). Thiadbod's man sells cloaks a hand short at the old price. Source: Notker, De Carolo Magno I.34 (tr. A. J. Grant 1907): Frisians sold short cloaks at the price of the long ones and the king forbade it; the Frank's line is Grant's wording, there said by Charles himself. Charles's letter to Offa, 796, on the length of cloaks (chronicle_793.json 796-spring-offa-letter). Cast: cast.thiadbod. From 795, after the debt's first reckonings (chain house_debt). Reads the spine's flag db_bought (counts_day): if the house's tally has been sold to Thiadbod he has what he wanted and this chain does not start; reads ch_house_debt_cleared for one line. Sets ch_house_rival_1 and one of ch_house_rival_short_cloth, ch_house_rival_true_cloth.

Source: Synod of Frankfurt, June 794, c. 4: oats 1 d the modius, barley 2, rye 3, wheat 4, by the new public modius, in plenty or dearth (MGH Capit. I no. 28; chronicle_793.json 794-06-01-frankfurt-prices); Nijmegen 806: oats 2, barley 3, rye 4, wheat 6, and hoarding for gain is 'turpe lucrum' (MGH Capit. I no. 46 c. 17-18; chronicle 806-03-nijmegen-prices). Cast: cast.thiadbod, cast.hartwin. Sets ch_house_rival_2, the timers ch_house_rival_rest (60 days) and ch_house_rival_wait (220 days), and the spine's hy_new_measure (hungry_years) where the player's measure is tried.

Source: Lex Frisionum, Additio sapientum VI (Saxmund): 'Si quis in flumine viam publicam occluserit, XII solidos componat'. Dorestad's dams and ditches: Design/content/dossiers/dorestad.md. Cast: cast.thiadbod (cast.gerlef named). Reads db_bought (the chain stops here if the tally was sold to him: chain house_debt, ending 'sold') and ch_house_debt_owed for one line. cards.note: Step 4 (scheduled 30 days after step 3, at Dorestad): the first wrecked boat, the player's own, cut from her post by night. The doer, Meinward (invented: Mein- + -ward, a half-free man of the Batua), has gone down river to Witla. Source: the hue and cry and the pledge taken by force are the ordinary law: Lex Frisionum, Additio VIII.2 ('pignoris nomine, quod pant dicunt'); a thing taken by force is paid twofold with 12 solidi for the peace (Tit. VIII). Sets ch_house_rival_4, the timer ch_house_rival_cutter_near (40 days) and one of ch_house_rival_cry, ch_house_rival_pant, ch_house_rival_quiet; schedules step 5 at Witla (two days down the river) and the court in forty nights (the Franks' term between courts (?)).

cards.note: Step 5, optional (scheduled by step 4: it opens on the first call at Witla from two days after the cut rope; nothing happens if she never calls there). The doer is kept in the pilot's shed for 40 days and then shipped oversea; a call after that finds him gone, and a call after the court finds only the pilot's shrug. The fork is the law's own: Lex Frisionum Tit. II, Wlemar's addition: if the doer has fled the land the setter-on pays a third or swears; if the doer has not fled, the setter 'neither swears nor pays, but only bears the enmity of him whose goods were taken'. So a man brought to court wins lawful enmity and no silver; a man heard before witnesses and let go oversea makes Thiadbod swear or pay. Witla: Design/content/dossiers/witla.md (nothing is known of the place but its burning in 836: the shed and the strand are ours). Cast: cast.gerlef. Sets ch_house_rival_5 and one of ch_house_rival_man_held, ch_house_rival_cutter_word, ch_house_rival_man_fled.

cards.note: Step 6 (scheduled forty nights after step 4, at Dorestad): the lawsuit at the thing, the count's court. Sources: Lex Frisionum Tit. III.3 (a free man charged with theft swears 'sua sexta manu'; if he owns it he pays twofold and his wergild to the king as fredus), III.8-9 (the ordeal of boiling water; a false accuser redeems his hand), Tit. II with Wlemar's addition (the setter-on), Tit. XIV.3 (between Vlie and Sincfal: the twelve-hand oath and boiling water), Additio VIII.2 (pant). Seven judgment-finders (scabini) are Charles's reform of about 780 (?); 'judges shall judge justly, according to the written law' is the capitulary of 802 c. 26 (tr. E. F. Henderson 1896); the peoples' laws were read and written at Aachen in October 802 (chronicle_793.json 802-10-aachen-laws-802). Where the court sat at Dorestad is not known: by Saint Martin's church is ours (?). The lawman's judgment on a boat ('a house on the water') is INVENTED: the real Lex has no word on ships; it sets changed_lex_frisionum_ship. Cast: cast.folcbert, cast.thiadbod; the lawman is an ordinary invented man. Sets ch_house_rival_6 and one of ch_house_rival_enmity, ch_house_rival_won, ch_house_rival_lost, ch_house_rival_porch.

Source: the law leaves the setter-on at enmity 'until he regains their friendship somehow' (Lex Frisionum Tit. II): friendship has a price. A widow holding her husband's storehouse is the spine's cast.thiadburg (the pattern is Frideburg of Birka, Rimbert c. 20). cards.note: Step 8 (drawn under way, from 100 days after step 7): the second wrecked boat, Thiadbod's big merchant ship on a bank that was not there at Easter. Sources: 'many ships wrecked with their crews by a violent storm in the British sea' in 799 (Historia Regum 799; chronicle_793.json 799-british-sea-storm), said only in that year; shifting banks at the Maas mouth (dossiers/witla.md); sword blades in a wine cask are the spine's fact about cast.thiadbod (thread swords_north: he sends blades north in wine casks), only seen here, not told. The danger warns first: the tide is making. Cast: cast.thiadbod; his son Thiadlef (invented: Thiad- + -lef), about fourteen. Sets ch_house_rival_8 and ch_house_rival_saved (with ch_house_rival_ship_saved or ch_house_rival_salvage) or ch_house_rival_left; ch_house_rival_saw_blades.

cards.note: Step 9 (scheduled 12 days after the bank, at Dorestad): the fork to the three endings. Whoever took the men off may offer fellowship; whoever did not float his ship may let the law and his losses run; anyone may declare the feud. Every state has a road that costs only pride. The ending is settled at the next court, forty nights on. Cast: cast.thiadbod, cast.thiadburg. Sets ch_house_rival_9.

cards.title: The reckoning
cards.intention: Thiadbod's wine was bought on trust, and the men he owes have come down to the dams. He and his sister are waiting for you.

options.label: Offer him fellowship: two boats, one reckoning
Let the law and his losses run, and be at the steward's sale
Say before witnesses that there is no peace between the houses

memory.law: let the law and his losses run
memory.feud: said there is no peace between the houses

cards.note: ENDING: partnership (scheduled forty nights after step 9, at Dorestad). Flag ch_house_rival_end_partner; grand reward unlock_partner_thiadbod; on the hard road (his ship floated, or nothing taken for the rescue, no pledge by force and no short cloth) also unlock_pilot_maas and changed_dorestad_fellowship. Sources: Capitulary of Herstal, 779, c. 16: no oaths sworn in guilds ('de sacramentis per gildonia invicem coniurantibus'), but men may make agreements for alms, for fire and for shipwreck without swearing (MGH Capit. I no. 20; from memory, the page could not be opened (?)); a sworn band is the lasting cost (ch_house_rival_sworn_band). Frisian guild-brothers are named on rune stones at Sigtuna in the 11th century (U 379, U 391) (?), and the merchants of Tiel 'swear and drink together' about 1020 (chronicle_793.json 1020-tiel-merchants): a chest for fire and wreck at Dorestad about 800 is HISTORY CHANGED. The upper church, Saint Martin's, is the Upkirika given to Utrecht in 777 (dossiers/dorestad.md). The verse is Havamal 47 (Bellows 1923; texts_793.json havamal_047). Cast: cast.thiadbod.

cards.note: ENDING: ruin (scheduled forty nights after step 9, at Dorestad). Flag ch_house_rival_end_ruin; grand reward unlock_plot_dorestad (the dam head), or unlock_ship_north_sea_merchant_ship (his hull, if he was left on the bank), or unlock_factor_dorestad (his sister keeps the dam head and your goods), or on the hard road (men saved and the case won) unlock_plot_dorestad with unlock_factor_mogontia. Lasting cost: ch_house_rival_sons_remember. This is the ordinary end of a merchant who loses a ship laden on trust: nothing changed. Sources: Dorestad's dam parcels and storehouses (dossiers/dorestad.md: 18 m parcels, dams up to 200 m); Frisian merchants living at Mainz, 'the best part of the city, where the Frisians lived' (Annales Fuldenses 886; dossiers/mogontia.md); arms out of the realm forbidden (Herstal 779, Thionville 805: chronicle_793.json). The sale of a debtor's goods by the count's steward is ours (?). Thiadbod's house is broken, not ended: the spine has his heirs at Dorestad to 863. Cast: cast.hartwin (to 808), cast.thiadbod.

cards.note: ENDING: feud (scheduled forty nights after step 9, at Dorestad). Flag ch_house_rival_end_feud; the lasting cost feud_house_thiadbod, which the heirs inherit (card s13); grand reward unlock_title_st_martins_man (the bishop's protection, with the debt of honour ch_house_rival_owes_martin_wax), or unlock_ship_north_sea_merchant_ship (his hull kept by the strong hand, if he was left on the bank), or unlock_heirloom_cut_rope. Sources: Lex Frisionum, Additio sapientum I.1 (Wlemar): 'Homo faidosus pacem habeat in ecclesia, in domo sua, ad ecclesiam eundo, de ecclesia redeundo, ad placitum eundo, de placito redeundo'; who breaks it and kills pays nine times 30 solidi. Capitulary of 802 c. 32: the kin 'shall by no means dare to carry further their enmity ... but, pledging their faith, they shall make a lasting peace' (tr. Henderson 1896); Thionville, December 805, c. 5: feuds to be settled (chronicle_793.json 805-12-thionville-arms). Saint Martin's men on Dorestad's banks owed no dues, and no one might lodge in their houses or seize their goods (Louis the Pious for Utrecht, 18 March 815, confirming older grants: Oorkondenboek Sticht Utrecht I no. 56, in dossiers/dorestad.md); for the years before 815 (?). Wreck kept as the finder's by 'the custom of the strand' is later law (?). The verse is Havamal 43 (Bellows 1923; texts_793.json havamal_043). Cast: cast.folcbert, cast.thiadbod; the bishop is cast.hamacar (to 806), here only his clerk.

cards.note: Epilogue of the feud ending (drawn at Dorestad from 826, when Thiadbod is dead, for the player's heir: generation 1 or later, while feud_house_thiadbod stands). The feud has outlived both men; the heirs meet where the law gives them peace. Sets ch_house_rival_heirs and either ch_house_rival_end_feud_healed (with feud_house_thiadbod = 0; a marriage gives unlock_kin_thiadbods_house and unlock_partner_thiadlef) or ch_house_rival_feud_kept. Sources: the peace of the man at feud in church and on the way to it (Additio sapientum I.1); the capitulary of 802 c. 32 on taking the price and making a lasting peace; a marriage to end a feud is the old custom the poems know (Beowulf 2020-2031, Freawaru given to Ingeld to settle the feud: texts_793.json has the poem by fitt). The Danes at Dorestad from 834: chronicle_793.json. The rival role's holder at Dorestad after 825 is Thiadbod's heir (the registry gives a fixed role to an heir with half the feelings).
